L.46: If I speak truth, why do you not believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

R.46: If I am telling you the truth, then why do you not believe {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

decisions.choice: if I speak truth: a real condition; since no fault can be shown, the question is why they do not believe
decisions.reason: The question has no answer they can give; Jesus himself answers it in 8:47.

decisions.choice: speak truth (no article)
decisions.reason: Here the Greek has "truth" without the article, unlike 8:45; Literal shows it. Balanced and Readable say "the truth", as English does.

records.source: ὁ ὢν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ θεοῦ ἀκούει· διὰ τοῦτο ὑμεῖς οὐκ ἀκούετε ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἐστέ.
records.gloss: The [one] being of the God the words of the God hears; for this you not hear, because of the God not you are."

L.47: The one who is of God hears the words of God; for this reason you do not hear, because you are not of God."

R.47: People who belong to God listen to God's words. But you do not listen to them, because you do not belong to God."

decisions.choice: of God: belonging to God, born of him
decisions.reason: To be "of God" is to have one's life from God (1:12-13; 3:3-8) and so to share his character; the same language is in 1 John 3:10 and 4:6. A person's response to God's words shows where he comes from.

decisions.choice: hear: listen and accept
decisions.reason: As in 8:43, hearing means taking the words to heart. They hear Jesus speak but do not receive what he says.

decisions.choice: you are not of God: said to these hearers, who reject the words of the one God sent
alternatives: a statement about the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: The "you" is the same group as in 8:37-44: those in the crowd who are seeking to kill him and will not hear him. It is a judgment on their present response, not on a people: in John, Jews in Jerusalem keep coming to believe (8:30; 11:45; 12:11, 42).

decisions.choice: comes from God (B); belong to God (R)
decisions.reason: "Is of God" (Literal) is not everyday English. Balanced says where such a person comes from, Readable whom they belong to; both are part of the sense (meaning decision m1).

records.source: Ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Οὐ καλῶς λέγομεν ἡμεῖς ὅτι Σαμαρίτης εἶ σὺ καὶ δαιμόνιον ἔχεις;
records.gloss: Answered the Jews and said to him, "Not well say we that a Samaritan are you and a demon you have?"

L.48: The Jews answered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do we not say rightly that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a Samaritan and have a demon?"

R.48: The Jews who were arguing with Jesus answered, "We are right about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, are we not? You are a Samaritan, and a demon has driven {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mad!"

decisions.choice: the Jews: the hearers in the temple courts who were disputing with Jesus, the same group as in 8:31-47
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: They answer what Jesus has just said to them (8:44-47). John introduced them in 8:31 as Jews who had believed him, and by 8:37 and 8:40 Jesus says they are seeking to kill him. The setting is the temple (8:20, 59). The word names this group of hearers, not the people as a whole: Jesus is himself a Jew (4:9, 22), and so are his disciples.

decisions.choice: Samaritan: an insult, branding him an outsider to Abraham's people
alternatives: a claim about where he was born
decisions.reason: They knew he came from Galilee (7:41, 52). Jews and Samaritans had long been divided (4:9), and Jews held that the Samaritans worshiped wrongly (4:20-22). To call a Jew a Samaritan was to say that he did not belong to Israel and taught falsely. It throws back his charge that they are not Abraham's true children (8:39-40).

decisions.choice: you have a demon: you are raving, in the grip of an evil spirit
decisions.reason: As in 7:20 and 10:20, the charge means that he is out of his mind. Here it also throws back his words of 8:44: he said that their father is the devil; they say that a demon is in him.

decisions.choice: Are we not right: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question with "not" expects agreement, and "we" is stressed: they claim they have been right about him all along (compare 7:20).

decisions.choice: the Jews who were arguing with him (B); the Jews who were arguing with Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this dispute (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote, as 8:31 does, and tie it to the people present, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew.

decisions.choice: a demon has driven you mad (R)
alternatives: you are out of your mind (as 7:20)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the insult (meaning decision m3), as 7:20 does, but keeps the demon, because Jesus answers that very word in verse 49 and it throws back his words about the devil (8:44).

records.heading: Before Abraham was

records.source: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγὼ δαιμόνιον οὐκ ἔχω, ἀλλὰ τιμῶ τὸν πατέρα μου, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀτιμάζετέ με.
records.gloss: Answered Jesus, "I a demon not have, but I honor the Father of me, and you dishonor me.

L.49: Jesus answered, "I do not have a demon, but I honor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and you dishonor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.49: Jesus answered, "I do not have a demon. I give honor to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and you are insulting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: I do not have a demon: he answers the second charge only
decisions.reason: Jesus does not trouble to deny that he is a Samaritan. The charge that matters is that his words come from an evil power. The stressed "I" sets him against his accusers, and the stressed "you" at the end answers it.

decisions.choice: honor and dishonor: giving or refusing the respect a person is due
decisions.reason: Honor was a person's public standing, and an insult took it away. Jesus speaks what the Father has taught him and does what pleases him (8:28-29), so in speaking he honors the Father; their insult falls on the one who sent him as well (5:23).

decisions.choice: Rather
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the denial its own sentence and lets "Rather" carry the contrast of the Greek "but".

decisions.choice: give honor to, are insulting (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the pair (meaning decision m2).

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ ζητῶ τὴν δόξαν μου· ἔστιν ὁ ζητῶν καὶ κρίνων.
records.gloss: I but not seek the glory of me; is the [one] seeking and judging.

L.50: But I do not seek {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory; there is one who seeks [it] and judges.

R.50: I am not trying to get glory for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}. But there is one who wants glory for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the judge.

decisions.choice: my glory: honor, a good name
decisions.reason: Here glory is the honor a person seeks or receives, as in 5:41-44 and 7:18: one who seeks his own glory speaks on his own authority. It carries on the talk of honor in verse 49.

decisions.choice: the one who seeks and judges: the Father, who upholds the Son's honor and decides between him and his accusers
decisions.reason: Verse 54 names him: it is the Father who glorifies the Son. "Judges" here means that he will decide the case between Jesus and those who dishonor him. In 5:22 the Father has given all judging to the Son; here the Father is the one who vindicates the Son (compare 8:16, 29).

decisions.choice: seeks: the object is understood from the first half
decisions.reason: The Greek gives no object for "seeks"; it is "my glory" carried over from the first half.

decisions.choice: [it] (L); it, he judges (B); wants glory for me, he is the judge (R)
decisions.reason: English needs the object that the Greek leaves understood (meaning decision m3). Readable says plainly whose glory is meant, without naming the Father, which Jesus leaves to verse 54.

records.source: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐάν τις τὸν ἐμὸν λόγον τηρήσῃ, θάνατον οὐ μὴ θεωρήσῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
records.gloss: Truly truly I say to you, if anyone the my word keeps, death not not will see into the age."

L.51: Truly, truly I say to you, if anyone keeps {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, {{gender:they|he}} will never see death."

R.51: I tell you the truth: anyone who holds on to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching and obeys it will never see death."

decisions.choice: keeps my word: holds to his teaching and obeys it
decisions.reason: To keep a word is to hold on to it and live by it (14:23; 15:20; 17:6). It takes up 8:31, "if you remain in my word". "Word" is his whole message, which they cannot bear to hear (8:37, 43).

decisions.choice: see death: experience death
decisions.reason: To "see death" is a Hebrew way of saying to die (Psalm 89:49; Luke 2:26; Hebrews 11:5). Jesus speaks of death as the end of life with God: whoever believes has passed from death to life (5:24), and will live even though he dies (11:25-26). He does not promise escape from bodily dying, but his hearers take it so (verse 52).

decisions.choice: never: the strongest denial, for all time
decisions.reason: Two negatives stand together, the strongest way of denying that something will happen, and "to the age" adds "for all time" (as in 10:28 and 11:26).

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 8:58 as well.

decisions.choice: if anyone ..., they (default) or he (traditional)
decisions.reason: "Anyone" means any person, man or woman; the gender setting gives the traditional "he". Readable says "anyone who" and needs no pronoun.

decisions.choice: holds on to my teaching and obeys it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what keeping his word means (meaning decision m1).

records.source: εἶπον αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Νῦν ἐγνώκαμεν ὅτι δαιμόνιον ἔχεις.
records.gloss: Said to him the Jews, "Now we have known that a demon you have.

L.52: The Jews said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Now we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have a demon.

R.52: The Jews there said to Jesus, "Now we are sure that a demon has driven {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mad.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the same hearers as in verse 48
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: The dispute goes on with the same people who were arguing with Jesus in the temple courts (8:31-48). Not the people as a whole: Jesus and his disciples are Jews.

decisions.choice: now we know: his last words have settled it for them
decisions.reason: The perfect tense means "we have come to know, and are sure". "Now" points to what he has just said (verse 51): to them the claim proves the charge of verse 48.

decisions.choice: the Jews there (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this dispute (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote, as 8:31 does, and tie it to the people present, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew.

decisions.choice: a demon has driven you mad
decisions.reason: As in verse 48 (rendering decision r-en-2 there).

records.source: Ἀβραὰμ ἀπέθανεν καὶ οἱ προφῆται, καὶ σὺ λέγεις· Ἐάν τις τὸν λόγον μου τηρήσῃ, οὐ μὴ γεύσηται θανάτου εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα·
records.gloss: Abraham died and the prophets, and you say, 'If anyone the word of me keeps, not not will he taste of death into the age';

L.52: Abraham died, and the prophets, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say, 'If anyone keeps {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, {{gender:they|he}} will never taste death.'

R.52: Abraham died, and so did the prophets. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say that anyone who obeys {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching will never die.

decisions.choice: taste death: experience death, die
decisions.reason: "Taste death" is another way of saying to die (Mark 9:1; Hebrews 2:9). In quoting Jesus they change "see" to "taste", but the sense is the same. The quotation is otherwise close to his words of verse 51.

decisions.choice: Abraham died: they take his words of bodily death
alternatives: they deny any life after death
decisions.reason: As often in John, the hearers take Jesus's words at the bodily level (3:4; 4:11; 6:52). Abraham and the prophets were the greatest of God's servants, and they died; how can this man's word do what theirs could not? Jesus spoke of the death that cuts a person off from God (verse 51, meaning decision m2 there).

decisions.choice: if anyone ..., they (default) or he (traditional)
decisions.reason: As in verse 51.

decisions.choice: you say that anyone who obeys your teaching will never die
alternatives: a direct quotation, as in Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Readable reports the words instead of quoting them and gives the plain sense of "taste death" (meaning decision m1).

records.source: μὴ σὺ μείζων εἶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ, ὅστις ἀπέθανεν;
records.gloss: Not you greater are than the father of us Abraham, who died?

L.53: Surely {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are not greater than our father Abraham, who died?

R.53: Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} think {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are greater than our father Abraham? He died.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The question is framed to expect "no". John's readers know the answer is yes; the Samaritan woman asked the same of Jacob (4:12).

decisions.choice: who died: great as he was, he died
decisions.reason: The relative pronoun has the sense "one who, for all his greatness, died". Death is their whole point: if Abraham could not escape it, no one can promise others they will.

decisions.choice: our father Abraham: the ancestor of Israel
decisions.reason: Abraham was the father of the nation, and their descent from him was their boast (8:33, 39). The chapter has turned on who their father truly is (8:38-44).

decisions.choice: Do you think you are greater
alternatives: Surely you are not greater (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the expected answer "no" (meaning decision m1) in words young readers know. It keeps "father", not "ancestor" as in 4:12, because the talk of fathers runs through this chapter.

records.source: καὶ οἱ προφῆται ἀπέθανον· τίνα σεαυτὸν ποιεῖς;
records.gloss: And the prophets died; whom yourself do you make?"

L.53: And the prophets died. Whom do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} [to be]?"

R.53: The prophets died too. Who do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} claim to be?"

decisions.choice: make yourself: claim to be, without right
alternatives: what are you trying to become
decisions.reason: They accuse him of claiming a rank that is not his, as in 5:18 ("making himself equal to God"), 10:33 and 19:7. John's irony: Jesus makes himself nothing; it is the Father who glorifies him (verse 54).

decisions.choice: and the prophets died: the point of verse 52 repeated
decisions.reason: They repeat the prophets' death to drive home the challenge. The question that follows is a rebuke, not a request for information.

decisions.choice: Who do you think you are (B); Who do you claim to be (R)
alternatives: Whom do you make yourself [to be] (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the everyday form of the challenge; Readable says plainly what they accuse him of (meaning decision m1).

records.source: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Ἐὰν ἐγὼ δοξάσω ἐμαυτόν, ἡ δόξα μου οὐδέν ἐστιν· ἔστιν ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ δοξάζων με, ὃν ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐστιν, καὶ οὐκ ἐγνώκατε αὐτόν, ἐγὼ δὲ οἶδα αὐτόν· κἂν εἴπω ὅτι οὐκ οἶδα αὐτόν, ἔσομαι ὅμοιος ὑμῖν ψεύστης· ἀλλὰ οἶδα αὐτὸν καὶ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ τηρῶ.
records.gloss: Answered Jesus, "If I glorify myself, the glory of me nothing is; is the Father of me the [one] glorifying me, whom you say that 'God of us he is,' \v 55 and not you have known him, I but know him; and if I say that not I know him, I will be like to you a liar; but I know him and the word of him I keep.

L.54: Jesus answered, "If I glorify {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory is nothing. It is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who glorifies {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, of whom you say, 'He is our God.'
L.55: And you have not known {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but I know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And if I were to say that I do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, I would be a liar like you. But I know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word.

R.54: Jesus answered, "If I give glory to {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, that glory is worth nothing. It is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glory. You say, 'He is our God.'
R.55: But you have never known {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. If I said that I did not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, I would be a liar, just like you. But I do know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and I obey what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says.

decisions.choice: glorify: honor that comes from God, not honor a person claims
decisions.reason: Glory a person gives himself is empty (5:41-44; 7:18). The Father glorifies the Son: in his signs (11:4), and above all in his "hour", his death and return to the Father (12:23; 13:31-32; 17:1, 5). It answers their question "Who do you make yourself out to be?" (verse 53).

decisions.choice: our God (SBLGNT): their own words, quoted
alternatives: "your God" (some manuscripts): Jesus's words about them
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts read "your God", so that Jesus says in his own words whom they call God. The SBLGNT reads "our God", and the word "that" then introduces their own words. The sense is the same either way. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: have known, know: two verbs, one meaning
decisions.reason: John uses both verbs for knowing God (7:28-29; 17:3, 25), and the change here is most likely for variety. The perfect "you have not known" says they have never come to know him; Jesus knows him as the one who comes from him (7:29).

decisions.choice: if I were to say ... I would be: a supposition he rejects
decisions.reason: To deny that he knows the Father would make him a liar, like those who claim God as Father but do not know him. It recalls 8:44, where the devil is a liar and the father of lies.

decisions.choice: keep his word: obey what the Father says
decisions.reason: Jesus does himself what he asks of others (verse 51): he keeps the Father's word, as his disciples are to keep his (15:10).

decisions.choice: give glory to, gives me glory; obey what he says (R)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key term as "glory" in a phrase young readers know, and spells out "keep his word" (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: were to say ... would be (L); said ... would be (B, R)
alternatives: if I say ... I will be
decisions.reason: English marks the supposition as unreal (meaning decision m4); the Greek future "I will be" is put as "I would be".

records.source: Ἀβραὰμ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἠγαλλιάσατο ἵνα ἴδῃ τὴν ἡμέραν τὴν ἐμήν, καὶ εἶδεν καὶ ἐχάρη.
records.gloss: Abraham the father of you rejoiced that he might see the day the my, and he saw and was glad."

L.56: Abraham your father rejoiced that he might see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} day, and he saw [it] and was glad."

R.56: Your father Abraham was full of joy because he was going to see the day when I would come. He saw it, and he was glad."

decisions.choice: rejoiced that he might see: joy looking ahead to what he would see
decisions.reason: The verb of great joy is followed by "that he might see", which points to something still ahead of him. The second half says that he did see it.

decisions.choice: my day: the time of Jesus's coming and work
alternatives: the day of judgment at the end
only the day of his death and rising
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of "the day of the Lord"; Jesus speaks of "my day", the time when he would come and do the Father's work. The phrase is not defined further, and it may take in his whole coming.

decisions.choice: he saw it: Abraham saw the day ahead, in God's promise
alternatives: he saw it from beyond death, in Jesus's own lifetime
he saw it in a vision
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say when or how Abraham saw it. Scripture gives Abraham the promise that all nations would be blessed through his offspring (Genesis 12:3; 22:18), and at the binding of Isaac he said that God would provide (Genesis 22:8, 14). His laughter at the promise of a son (Genesis 17:17) was read by some ancient Jewish interpreters as joy. Hebrews 11:13 says that the fathers saw what was promised from far off and welcomed it. Any of these may lie behind the saying; marked uncertain.

decisions.choice: your father: their ancestor by descent
decisions.reason: Jesus grants that they are Abraham's descendants (8:37), though he has denied that they act as his children (8:39-40). Abraham welcomed the day they now reject.

decisions.choice: was full of joy at the hope of seeing ... it made him glad
alternatives: rejoiced that he might see ... was glad (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the two verbs of joy in natural English and shows that the first looks ahead (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: the day when I would come
decisions.reason: Readable says what "my day" refers to (meaning decision m2). It names his coming in general, without choosing among the views of when Abraham saw it.

records.source: εἶπον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι πρὸς αὐτόν· Πεντήκοντα ἔτη οὔπω ἔχεις καὶ Ἀβραὰμ ἑώρακας;
records.gloss: Said therefore the Jews to him, "Fifty years not yet you have, and Abraham you have seen?"

L.57: So the Jews said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You are not yet fifty years [old], and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have seen Abraham?"

R.57: So the Jews there said to Jesus, "You are not even fifty years old. How could {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have seen Abraham?"

decisions.choice: the Jews: the same hearers as in verses 48 and 52
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: The same people who were arguing with Jesus in the temple courts. Not the people as a whole: Jesus and his disciples are Jews.

decisions.choice: not yet fifty: a round figure for a man not yet old
alternatives: a guess at his actual age
decisions.reason: They are not stating his age but saying he is far too young to have known Abraham. Fifty marked full maturity: Levites served until that age (Numbers 4:3; 8:24-25). Luke 3:23 says Jesus was about thirty when he began his work.

decisions.choice: and you have seen Abraham? (SBLGNT)
alternatives: "and has Abraham seen you?" (a few manuscripts, among them P75 and the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus)
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts, some of them early, have Abraham as the one who sees, which is closer to what Jesus said in verse 56. The SBLGNT reading has the hearers turn his words around: he had said that Abraham saw his day. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Jews there (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this dispute (meaning decision m1), not the authorities alone and not the Jewish people as a whole. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote, as 8:31 does, and tie it to the people present, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew.

decisions.choice: two sentences, with "How could you have seen"
alternatives: and you have seen Abraham? (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the scorn of the question plain.

records.source: εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, πρὶν Ἀβραὰμ γενέσθαι ἐγὼ εἰμί.
records.gloss: Said to them Jesus, "Truly truly I say to you, before Abraham to come to be, I am."

L.58: Jesus said to them, "Truly, truly I say to you, before Abraham came to be, I am."

R.58: Jesus said to them, "I tell you the truth: before Abraham was even born, I am."

decisions.choice: came to be / I am: a beginning set against being without beginning
alternatives: only that Jesus existed earlier than Abraham
decisions.reason: For Abraham Jesus uses a verb of coming into being; for himself he does not say "I was" but the present "I am". The same contrast opens the Gospel: the Word "was" in the beginning, while all things "came to be" through him (1:1-3).

decisions.choice: I am: the words with which God names himself
alternatives: only a claim to have lived before Abraham
decisions.reason: The words stand with no predicate. God names himself "I am" (Exodus 3:14), and in the Greek of Isaiah he says "I am" of himself (Isaiah 41:4; 43:10-13). In 6:20 the plain sense "it is I" was uppermost, and in 8:24 and 8:28 the words were veiled; here no plain sense fits. The hearers' answer in verse 59 shows how they understood him: the law's penalty for blasphemy was stoning (Leviticus 24:16; compare 10:31-33). A footnote notes the echo.

decisions.choice: I am (every level)
decisions.reason: The book's terms keep "before Abraham was, I am" at every level, so that the present tense and the echo of God's name (meaning decisions m1 and m2) stay visible. English can bear the change of tense; smoothing it would hide what the hearers reacted to.

decisions.choice: came to be (L); was (B); was even born (R)
decisions.reason: Literal shows the verb of coming into being; Balanced keeps the book's wording "before Abraham was"; Readable says it plainly. Only the first half changes; every level ends with "I am".

records.source: ἦραν οὖν λίθους ἵνα βάλωσιν ἐπ’ αὐτόν· Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἐκρύβη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ.
records.gloss: They took up therefore stones that they might throw at him; Jesus but was hidden and went out from the temple.

L.59: So they picked up stones to throw at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; but Jesus hid {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} and went out of the temple.

R.59: Then they picked up stones to throw at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But Jesus hid {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} and went out of the temple area.

decisions.choice: picking up stones: to put him to death for blasphemy
decisions.reason: Stoning was the law's penalty for blasphemy (Leviticus 24:16). They act at once, without a trial, as they will try to do again in 10:31-33. It shows how they understood "I am" in verse 58.

decisions.choice: hid himself: a passive form with a reflexive sense
alternatives: was hidden, by God or by the crowd
decisions.reason: The form is passive, but verbs like this often have the sense of doing something to oneself, and John uses the same form in 12:36, "he went away and hid himself from them". John does not say how he escaped. His hour had not yet come (7:30; 8:20). A footnote gives "was hidden".
